content.sanskrit: ओमित्येतदक्षरमिदं सर्वं तस्योपव्याख्यानं भूतं भवद्भविष्यदिति सर्वमोंकार एव । यच्चान्यत् त्रिकालातीतं तदप्योंकार एव ॥
content.transliteration: omityetadakṣaramidaṁ sarvaṁ tasyopavyākhyānaṁ bhūtaṁ bhavadbhaviṣyaditi sarvamoṁkāra eva | yaccānyat trikālātītaṁ tadapyoṁkāra eva ||
content.text:
Om ! — This syllable is this whole world.

Its further explanation is : —

The past, the present, the future — everything is just the
word Om.

And whatever else that transcends threefold time 2 — that, too,
is just the word Om.

content.transliteration: sarvaṁ hyetadbrahm āyamātmā brahma so'yamātmā catuṣpāt |
content.text:
For truly, everything here is Brahma ; this self ( dtman ) is
Brahma. This same self has four fourths.

content.sanskrit: जागरितस्थानो बहिष्प्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः स्थूलभुग्वैश्वानरः प्रथमः पादः ॥
content.transliteration: jāgaritasthāno bahiṣprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṁśatimukhaḥ sthūlabhugvaiśvānaraḥ prathamaḥ pādaḥ ||
content.text:
The waking state {jagarita-sthana), outwardly cognitive,
having seven limbs,3 having nineteen mouths,4 enjoying the
gross ( stJiula-bhuj ), the Common-to-all-men ( vaisvanara ), is
the first fourth.

content.sanskrit: स्वप्नस्थानोऽन्तःप्रज्ञः सप्ताङ्ग एकोनविंशतिमुखः प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजसो द्वितीयः पादः ॥
content.transliteration: svapnasthāno'ntaḥprajñaḥ saptāṅga ekonaviṁśatimukhaḥ praviviktabhuktaijaso dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ ||
content.text:
The dreaming state ( svapna-sthana ), inwardly cognitive,
having seven limbs, having nineteen mouths, enjoying the
exquisite ( pravivikta-bhuj ), the Brilliant ( taijasa ), is the second
fourth.

content.sanskrit: यत्र सुप्तो न कञ्चन कामं कामयते न कञ्चन स्वप्नं पश्यति तत्सुषुप्तम् ।
content.transliteration: yatra supto na kañcana kāmaṁ kāmayate na kañcana svapnaṁ paśyati tatssuṣuptam |
content.text:
If one asleep desires no desire whatsoever, sees no dream
whatsoever.1 2 that is deep sleep (sitsupta).

The deep-sleep state ( susnpta-st/iana. ), unified (eki-bhuta)?
just (eva.) a cognition-mass ( prajnana-ghana ),3 consisting of
bliss ( ananda-maya ),4 enjoying bliss (ananda-b/mj) , whose
mouth is thought (cetas-), the Cognitional ( prdjiia ), is the
third fourth.

content.sanskrit: एष सर्वेश्वरः एष सर्वज्ञ एषोऽन्तर्याम्येष योनिः सर्वस्यप्रभवाप्ययौ हि भूतानाम्
content.text:
This is the lord of all (sarvesvai'a).5 This is the all-
knowing ( sarva-jna)P This is the inner controller ( aiitar -
yamin ).7 This is the source ( yotti ) 8 of all, for this is the
origin and the end ( prabhavapyayau) 9 of beings.

content.sanskrit: नान्तःप्रज्ञं न बहिष्प्रज्ञं नोभयतःप्रज्ञं न प्रज्ञानघनं न प्रज्ञं नाप्रज्ञम् ।
content.transliteration: nāntaḥprajñaṁ na bahiṣprajñaṁ nobhayataḥprajñaṁ na prajñānaghanaṁ na prajñaṁ nāprajñam |
content.text:
Not inwardly cognitive {antah-prajna), not outwardly
cognitive ( bahih-prajiia ), not both-wise cognitive ( iibhayatah -
prajna), not a cognition-mass ( prajuana-gJiana), not cognitive
(pj'ajiia), not non-cognitive ( a-prajiia ), unseen (a-drsta), with
which there can be no dealing ( a-zyavahdrya ), ungraspable (a-
grahya ), having no distinctive mark (a-laksatia), non-thinkable
( a-cintya ), that cannot be designated (a-vyapadcsya) ,the essence
of the assurance of which is the state of being one with the
Self10 (ekdtinya-pratyaya-sara), the cessation of development
( prapancopasama ), tranquil (santa)> benign (siva), without a
second ( a-dvaita ) — [such] they think is the fourth.11 He is
the Self (Atman). He should be discerned.

content.sanskrit: सोऽयमात्माध्यक्षरमोङ्करोऽधिमात्रं पादा मात्रा मात्राश्च पादाअकार उकारो मकार इति
content.text:
This is the Self with regard to the word Oju, with
regard to its elements. The elements ( matra ) are the fourths ;

content.sanskrit: जागरितस्थानो वैश्वानरोऽकारः प्रथमा मात्राऽऽप्तेरादिमत्त्वाद्वाऽऽप्नोति ह वै सर्वान् कामानादिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
content.text:
The waking state, the Common-to-all-mcn, is the letter a ,
the first element, from apli (‘ obtaining ’) or from adimatvd
(‘ being first ’).

He obtains, verily, indeed, all desires, he becomes first — he
who knows this.

content.sanskrit: स्वप्नस्थानस्तैजस उकारो द्वितीया मात्रोत्कर्षात्उभयत्वाद्वोत्कर्षति ह वै ज्ञानसन्ततिं समानश्च भवतिनास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति य एवं वेद
content.text:
The sleeping state, the Brilliant, is the letter u, the
second element, from utkarsa (‘ exaltation ’) or from ubhayatvd
(‘ intermediateness ’).

He exalts, verily, indeed, the continuity of knowledge ;
and he becomes equal 3 ( samana ) ; no one ignorant of Brahma
is born in the family of him who knows this.

content.sanskrit: सुषुप्तस्थानः प्राज्ञो मकारस्तृतीया मात्रा मितेरपीतेर्वामिनोति ह वा इदं सर्वमपीतिश्च भवति य एवं वेद
content.text:
The deep- sleep state, the Cognitional, is the letter in,
the third element, from miti (‘erecting’) or from apitp
(■ immerging ’).

He, verily, indeed, erects ( minoti ) this whole world,4 and he
becomes its immerging — he who knows this.

content.sanskrit: अमात्रश्चतुर्थोऽव्यवहार्यः प्रपञ्चोपशमः शिवोऽद्वैतएवमोङ्कार आत्मैव संविशत्यात्मनाऽऽत्मानं य एवं वेद
content.text:
The fourth is without an element, with which there can
be no dealing, the cessation of development, benign, without a
second.

Thus Om is the Self (Atman) indeed.

He who knows this, with his self enters the Self — yea, he
who knows this!
